sources.title: Tagged SQL question projection and ownership

claims.text: The sources preserve only an SQL top-ten-by-grade student task plus MySQL/SQL/LIMIT classification; schema, score granularity, ranking/tie, NULL/no-score, version and output rules remain answer-side contracts.
Under the explicit one-final-score / at-most-ten-row contract, exact SQL joins by student_id, orders score DESC then student_id ASC and applies LIMIT 10.
The candidate distinguishes deterministic row cutoff from rank-with-ties semantics and requires a specified per-student aggregation metric before ranking multi-course rows.

validation.reported_stdout: PASS empty=0 small=5 top10=10 tie=cutoff-deterministic no-score=excluded

boundary_tests.case: 5 scored students plus one no-score student

boundary_tests.expected: excluded by explicit INNER JOIN contract

findings: The stronger OCR source preserves only an SQL task to find students with top-ten grades; the tagged projection adds MySQL/SQL/LIMIT classification, but neither source preserves schema, score granularity, tie, NULL/no-score, version or output rules.

The candidate explicitly scopes its primary query to one non-NULL final score per scored student, at most ten rows, INNER JOIN exclusion of no-score students, and student_id as deterministic cutoff tie-breaker.
The primary fenced SQL is byte-for-byte identical to the executable fixture and produces correct empty, fewer-than-ten, and greater-than-ten results.
A cutoff tie is deterministically resolved by score DESC then student_id ASC; the answer correctly states this is a row-limit policy, not a claim that equal scores have different mathematical rank.
The answer separates exactly-ten-row LIMIT semantics from top-ten rank levels including ties, and distinguishes RANK from DENSE_RANK for MySQL 8+ follow-up semantics.
The answer fail-closes the one-student-many-course case by requiring an explicit aggregation metric before ranking instead of guessing AVG or SUM.
No placeholder SQL, source-fabricated schema, fabricated production claim or uncovered preserved source requirement remains.
